page: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an ARM-based cloud instance powered by 8 dedicated physical cores running on first-generation AWS Graviton processors with Cortex-A72 microarchitecture at 2.3 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro system hypervisor, the instance incorporates 16.0 GB of RAM (providing 2.0 GB of memory per core), 32 KB of L1d cache, and 2 MB of L2 cache. The system supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions, operates without hyperthreading, and includes no bundled local NVMe SSD storage or GPU acceleration. Baseline network performance is rated at 2 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core CPU stress performance with a stress-ng multi-core result of 11904.08 and a single-core score of 1491.99. However, memory subsystem throughput remains limited, exhibiting read bandwidth of 23.51 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 8.88 GB/sec in large block tests. Single-threaded performance and mathematical instruction metrics fall in lower benchmark percentiles, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 410.0, a multi-core score of 2143.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 3170.47. Web serving throughput reaches 2.41 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance registers at 4.24 million operations per second.

The a1.2xlarge offers a entry-level, dedicated-core hardware profile tailored for ARM-native software stacks that do not require high memory bandwidth or specialized vector extensions like AVX. Dedicated vCPU execution avoids noisy-neighbor contention common in shared-core instances, though the legacy Cortex-A72 cores present trade-offs in intensive compute or compression tasks. Recommended workload fits include containerized ARM microservices, scale-out web server deployments, basic CI/CD execution nodes, and lightweight Redis caching environments.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.2xlarge is an ARM-based instance equipped with 8 dedicated AWS Graviton physical cores based on the Cortex-A72 architecture, operating at 2.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, hardware AES acceleration, and no local SSD storage. Benchmark evaluation shows average multi-core CPU performance in stress tests alongside weak memory bandwidth speeds, measured at 23.51 GB/sec read and 8.88 GB/sec write. Due to the first-generation Graviton architecture and modest single-threaded throughput, the instance exhibits lower performance in compute-heavy or vector-intensive applications. However, its dedicated core design offers predictable execution for lightweight, scale-out ARM workloads. It is best suited for basic web serving, containerized ARM microservices, lightweight Redis caching, and entry-level Linux cloud applications.

tagline: An eight-core ARM-based server instance with dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB memory optimized for entry-level scale-out workloads and containerized microservices.
bullet_points: 8 dedicated ARM Cortex-A72 physical cores operating at 2.3 GHz on AWS Nitro Hypervisor
16 GB system memory delivering a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without hyperthreading
2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support
EBS-only storage model with no bundled local NVMe SSDs or GPU accelerators
